title: MatrixDiagV3 primitive rejects documented Python int diagonal arguments
duplicate_search_queries: site:gitee.com/mindspore/mindspore/issues MatrixDiagV3 input[1] should be a Tensor got Int64
site:github.com/mindspore-ai/mindspore/issues MatrixDiagV3 input[1] should be a Tensor got Int64
duplicate_search_result: No exact matching GitHub or Gitee issue found for MatrixDiagV3 direct primitive Python int argument rejection.
documentation_notes: MindSpore 2.9 MatrixDiagV3 docs list k as Union[int, Tensor] and num_rows/num_cols/padding_value as scalar-compatible arguments, with CPU support.
The higher-level ops.matrix_diag wrapper accepts the same Python int arguments in both execution modes.
Tensor-valued MatrixDiagV3 primitive arguments pass, so the failure is localized to Python scalar handling in the direct primitive.
classification_notes: Not a numerical precision issue: the direct primitive raises before returning a tensor.
Not a CPU unsupported issue: Tensor-valued primitive controls and ops.matrix_diag Python-int controls pass on CPU.
Related to, but distinct from, MS-024: MS-024 covers matrix_diag_part k handling; this issue covers the direct MatrixDiagV3 primitive.
